subject: Pilot readiness: ops, unit economics and quantization signals
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Dunn <elliot.dunn@cleargate.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot readiness: ops, unit economics and quantization signals

Elliot — thanks again for the time today. Quick write-up from our side so we have the same next steps and success criteria captured. Feel free to correct anything I missed.

Key pain points you raised
- Token/unit economics: current spend on hosted LLMs has become cost-prohibitive for scaling new features (esp. around personalization + long context).
- Latency spikes during short transactional calls (search/assist) that need predictable p95s for the UX team.
- Ops overhead: managing model variants and fallbacks across regions is brittle; limited visibility into per-route token costs.

What we heard about your current stack
- Production mix: primary hosted model (third-party API) for safety/accuracy + in-house Llama2 13B cluster on k8s as fallback.
- Typical request profiles: ~60% short transactions (100-400 tokens), ~30% mid-context (1k-2k), ~10% long sessions (2k-6k).
- You currently batch at the application layer but have not tried KV prefix caching or model quantization in prod.

Success criteria for a pilot (your goals)
- Reduce per-1M-token spend by >40% for the nucleus of the workload (short + mid-context).
- Maintain or improve p95 latency for short transactions (target: <= 120ms p95).
- Demonstrate stable ops playbook (autoscale + graceful fallback) for 2 weeks of production traffic.

How Redwood can help (high level)
- Batching + dynamic latency windows: keep tail latencies low while improving GPU utilization.
- KV / prefix caching for session reuse (especially helpful for the 60% short transactions).
- Quantization profiles (int8/4-bit) with accuracy guardrails and simple rollout.
- Transparent cost model and per-route token breakdown to validate unit economics.

Proposed next steps
1) Technical deep-dive with your infra team (we suggested Mon 6/14) to look at traffic traces and token distribution.
2) You share a 48–72 hour sample traffic trace and 20 representative prompts (we can accept sanitized examples). Link to sample trace: https://drive.redwood.com/CLG-2387/sample-traffic-trace.csv
3) Redwood prepares a pilot MOP and a mutual action plan (attached: redwood-pilot-outline.pdf).
4) Run 2-week pilot with defined SLOs, quantization experiments, and ops runbook.

Open questions we left on the call
- How tolerant is the product team to minor latency variance during night-time batch windows?
- Any internal procurement timelines we should be aware of for Dedicated/Private options?

Attachments: redwood-pilot-outline.pdf (stub)

Thanks — I’ll coordinate schedules once you confirm your preferred time for the deep-dive.

—
Ben Carter
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192
From: Elliot Dunn <elliot.dunn@cleargate.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2026 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot readiness: ops, unit economics and quantization signals

Ben — thanks for the clear recap. Accurate for the most part; a few clarifications below.

Clarifications / extra detail
- Current spend: ballpark we’re at ~$4k/month for the user-facing model endpoints today, but expected to grow quickly as we onboard experimental personalization flows. The key metric for us is cost per monthly active user (MAU) for inference.
- Latency tolerance: product wants p95 <= 120ms for core flows; exploratory flows can be 300–500ms. Night-time batch windows are fine to shift more work if accuracy is preserved.
- Openness to quantization: willing to try 8-bit and 4-bit for non-critical paths; we need a quick regression test on top of our deterministic prompts to catch hallucination or scoring drift.

What I can prepare for the deep-dive
- 72-hour traffic trace (sanitized) and a short token distribution summary.
- A list of our top 50 prompts by frequency and a couple of failure examples.

Questions for Redwood before the deep-dive
- Do you have an example runbook for rollback if a quantized variant increases failure rate?
- What minimum telemetry/agent footprint do you need on our cluster for the pilot (we prefer not to open long-lived SSH).

Happy to take Mon 6/14 at 10:00am PT for the deep-dive — tentatively booked that slot on my calendar, unless you want a different time.

—
Elliot Dunn
Head of Product, ClearGate Analytics
elliot.dunn@cleargate.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Dunn <elliot.dunn@cleargate.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2026 08:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot readiness: ops, unit economics and quantization signals

Appreciate the context, Elliot — that helps. Short answers to your questions and a tightened next-steps list below.

Rollback & safety
- Example runbook: quick rollback is a tag-based model routing policy + canary traffic split (we keep original variant live for instant rollback). We'll bring a pre-built rollback playbook to the deep-dive.

Telemetry footprint
- Minimal agent: HTTP upload of aggregated metrics and traces; optional sidecar for streaming logs. No long-lived SSH required. We can run in read-only mode with a short-lived token for the pilot.

Pilot configuration proposal (high level)
- Duration: 2 weeks (can extend after results).
- Traffic split: start 5% of production traffic on canary quantized variants, expand to 25% if regression < 0.5% on your tests.
- Batching: dynamic batching with 25ms collection window plus locality-aware routing (keeps p95 low for short transactions).
- Caching: KV prefix caching for session reuse; expect 10–30% token reduction on short sessions depending on reuse.
- Quantization: staged (int8 -> 4-bit) for non-critical paths; hold critical scoring on fp16 until validated.

Deliverables before the deep-dive (we can prepare these by EOD Fri)
- Mutual action plan (attached) and a one-page cost model showing estimated $/1M tokens under three configs (baseline, batching+caching, batching+caching+quant).
- Runbook & rollback checklist.

I attached the mutual-action-plan.xlsx stub and included the Drive link you can upload trace to. If Mon 6/14 10:00am PT works, we’ll send a calendar invite with dial-in and a short agenda focused on: traffic shape, acceptance tests, telemetry requirements, access model.

Attachments: mutual-action-plan.xlsx (stub)

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.
